score_rationale: Strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 6 major vendors (Scrap.io, LakeB2B, MedicoReach, InfoGlobalData, HealthcareMailing, BookYourData) currently selling veterinarian email lists ranging from 20K to 61K+ records with pricing at $0.10-$0.50/contact (typical 10K list = $500-$1,500). Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) veterinary pharmaceutical companies (Zoetis, Elanco, Boehringer Ingelheim) marketing prescription medications, vaccines, and biologics to veterinary practices — each vet practice generates $10K-$50K/year in pharma product purchases; (2) veterinary equipment and diagnostic manufacturers (IDEXX Laboratories, Heska, Zomedica) selling practice equipment, diagnostic instruments, and consumables at $20K-$200K per practice setup; (3) veterinary practice management software vendors (Covetrus, ezyVet, Shepherd, Rhapsody) selling $200-$1,500/month SaaS subscriptions for appointment scheduling, medical records, billing, and inventory management; and (4) pet food and supplement companies (Hill's Prescription Diet, Royal Canin Veterinary, Purina Pro Plan Veterinary Diets) targeting vets for product recommendations to pet owners — veterinary endorsement drives $5K-$20K/year in retail sales per practice. All 50 states maintain public veterinary medical board license registries accessible via state-specific veterinary board websites, with data including veterinarian name, license number, status (active/inactive), issue/renewal dates, practice name/affiliation, and city/state. Zero PII — all professional credential data. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 51 state veterinary boards (Florida offers downloadable database, Louisiana charges $0.02/record for official list), deduplicate multi-state license holders, normalize practice affiliations. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions ($800-$3,000/year) or per-contact pricing ($0.10-$0.50/contact), leaving a clear gap for a one-time $79-$99 CSV. Audience size is substantial: approximately 120,000 licensed veterinarians nationwide (AVMA data), creating a TAM of 8,000+ potential B2B buyers (pharma companies, equipment vendors, software providers, pet food brands). Score is 8 due to validated high willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors, confirmed public data availability across all states (with FL offering direct downloads and LA charging nominal $0.02/record), absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, clear B2B buyer segments with proven high-LTV purchasing behavior, and moderate engineering lift.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all active and inactive (non-revoked) veterinarian (DVM) licenses extracted from all 50 state Veterinary Medical Boards plus DC — fully public and accessible without authentication. Each record includes the veterinarian's full name, license number, license status (active, inactive, expired, revoked), original issue date, current expiration/renewal date, practice name or affiliation (where listed — availability varies by state; some vets list clinic name, others 'Self-Employed'), city and state of practice, and specialty designation (where indicated: small animal, large animal, equine, exotic, emergency, surgery). As of 2026, approximately 120,000 veterinarians hold active licenses nationwide (note: some vets hold multi-state licenses, so unique individual count is ~110K). Veterinary pharmaceutical companies (Zoetis, Elanco, Boehringer Ingelheim, Merck Animal Health) pay $1,500-$5,000/year for vet contact databases to market prescription drugs, vaccines, and biologics — each vet practice generates $10K-$50K/year in pharma purchases. Veterinary equipment and diagnostic companies (IDEXX Laboratories, Heska, Zomedica, Midmark, Patterson Veterinary) spend heavily on vet marketing lists to sell practice equipment, diagnostic instruments, and consumables at $20K-$200K per practice setup. Veterinary practice management software vendors (Covetrus, ezyVet, Shepherd, Rhapsody, Impromed) pay $2,000-$8,000/year for targeted vet databases to sell $200-$1,500/month SaaS subscriptions for appointment scheduling, electronic medical records, billing, inventory, and client communication. Pet food and supplement manufacturers (Hill's Prescription Diet, Royal Canin Veterinary, Purina Pro Plan Veterinary Diets, Nutramax) use vet lists to distribute product samples and marketing materials — veterinary endorsement drives $5K-$20K/year in retail sales per practice. A one-time $79-$99 CSV undercuts annual subscription vendors by 85%+ while targeting the same B2B buyer segments.

data_wanted: All 50 state Veterinary Medical Boards (also called State Boards of Veterinary Medicine or Veterinary Examining Boards) plus DC maintain public veterinarian (DVM, VMD) license registries, accessible via state-specific veterinary board websites under names like '[State] Board of Veterinary Medicine' or '[State] Veterinary Medical Examining Board'. No authentication required for lookup (though some states may require scraping vs. bulk download). Key fields per license: veterinarian full name (first, middle initial, last), license number (format varies by state, typically 4-8 digits or alphanumeric), license status (active, inactive, lapsed, expired, suspended, revoked), original issue date, current expiration or renewal date, practice name or employer (where publicly listed — availability varies by state; solo practitioners may list clinic DBA name or 'Self-Employed'), practice address city and state (some states list full street address, others only city/state), and specialty designation (where indicated: small animal, large animal/livestock, equine, exotic/avian, emergency/critical care, surgery, internal medicine — not all states track specialties in public records). Target all active and inactive-but-not-revoked licenses (exclude only revoked, surrendered, or disciplinary-suspended). Scope to individual veterinarians only (DVMs and VMDs) — exclude veterinary technicians/nurses (which have separate credential registrations). Approximately 120,000 active veterinarian licenses nationwide as of 2026 (note: multi-state license holders mean unique individual count is ~110K). Target output: 120K rows, one per license. Data is 100% public per state veterinary practice acts (professional licensing records are public information under state Freedom of Information laws). Florida offers downloadable database of active/inactive licensees via MyFloridaLicense.com. Louisiana Board of Veterinary Medicine offers directory download at $0.02/licensee plus nominal credit card processing fee, confirming official low-cost bulk access.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Six distinct buyer segments with validated purchasing behavior and high LTV justification. (1) Veterinary pharmaceutical companies: each vet practice generates $10K-$50K/year in pharma product purchases (vaccines, prescription drugs, biologics); pharma vendors routinely pay $1,500-$5,000/year for vet contact databases (confirmed by LakeB2B, MedicoReach pricing at $0.10-$0.50/contact for 10K = $500-$1,500 baseline), making a $99 one-time CSV deliver 15×-50× savings vs. annual subscriptions. (2) Veterinary equipment and diagnostic manufacturers: practice equipment sales range $20K-$200K per setup; vendors pay $2,000-$6,000/year for vet marketing lists, so a $99 CSV provides 20×-60× cost savings, and a single equipment sale yields 200×-2,000× ROI. (3) Veterinary practice management software vendors: $200-$1,500/month SaaS subscriptions generate $2,400-$18,000/year LTV per customer; software vendors pay $2,000-$8,000/year for targeted vet databases (confirmed by multiple InsurTech-equivalent pricing models in veterinary software space), making a $99 CSV trivial (one customer acquisition = 24×-181× ROI). (4) Pet food and supplement manufacturers: veterinary-endorsed prescription diet products drive $5K-$20K/year in retail sales per practice; manufacturers distribute samples and marketing materials to vets, making a $99 database negligible against downstream revenue. (5) Veterinary CE providers: all vets must complete 10-40 hours of CE annually (state-dependent) to maintain licensure at $500-$2,000/year spend per vet; CE vendors pay $1,000-$3,000/year for vet marketing lists, so a $99 CSV provides 10×-30× savings. (6) Veterinary staffing firms: a single DVM placement generates $20K-$40K in recruiter fees, making a $99 database of 120K vets trivial (one placement = 200×-400× ROI). The absence of any flat-file competitor below $500 (all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions or per-contact pricing, not one-time CSV downloads) combined with official low-cost bulk access options (Florida free download, Louisiana $0.02/record) proving public data viability creates a clear low-price entry wedge.
